relics.name: Wick's Drawing
relics.lore: A crayon fish with too many legs. On the back, in a grown-up's handwriting: 'He draws them before they come.'

hint.text: Wick is drawing a fish he wants caught. He pays in drawings.

relics.name: The Keeper's Spectacles
relics.lore: Wire rims, gone sea-green. One lens is plain glass. Through the other the moon on the water has a twin, a little to the left, and the twin is the brighter.

hint.text: Wick: 'There's glasses in Lantern Cove. At night they look up. I drew them. I'm not going in.'

relics.name: The Keeper's Kettle
relics.lore: Dented tin, a rope handle. It has sat on a bare rock for twelve winters and it is warm. It is always nearly boiling.

hint.text: Pell: 'The keeper took her tea on an isle to the south-west, tides she wanted quiet. The kettle will be there yet.'

relics.name: A Cork Float With Two Names
relics.lore: Off a child's pot line. MARA, in knife-cut capitals, and under it, smaller and neater, I. Somebody has started to sand the I away and thought better of it.

hint.text: Mara: 'We had a pot line off the Teeth, as girls. I had. One of the floats went adrift and I never looked very hard.'

relics.name: Next Year's Tide Table
relics.lore: Pell's hand, ruled in pencil, for a year that has not happened. Every tide in it so far has been right. One date is underlined twice and he will not say whose it is.

hint.text: Pell: 'I let my tables go over the side, out in the open water. Next year's. You'll find them last spring.'

relics.name: A Ticket for the Fen Packet
relics.lore: One single, Hearthbay to Sedge Landing, first boat. It has been punched. The date on it is the day after tomorrow, and by the look of the card it has been the day after tomorrow for forty years.

hint.text: Mara: 'The packet went at first light, off the end of our dock. People dropped all sorts, getting aboard half asleep.'

relics.name: A Jar of Fen Light
relics.lore: A preserving jar, the lid waxed down. It was empty when it came up. It is brighter with the lid on, and brightest when you are not looking straight at it.

hint.text: Dr. Calloway: 'Somebody was bottling the glow, under the Standing Trees. I found the wax and the string. Not the jars. I looked by day, of course.'

relics.name: Calloway's Tape Measure
relics.lore: Brass case, linen tape. It gave the same answer twice in a row, once, and she handed it over at once. 'I should rather not know which of us was right.'

hint.text: Dr. Calloway has something put by for whoever fills the journal's Mossglass page.

relics.name: A Second Page of Isolde's Logbook
relics.lore: 'Let the lead down the Sump. Ran out of line at ninety fathom and felt it taken, gently, the way you take a cup from someone who has fallen asleep holding it. It was not a fish. I think it was being kind.'

hint.text: Dr. Calloway: 'My lead came up from the Sump once with ruled paper on the hook. Handwriting. I let it go down again before I could read it. On principle.'

relics.name: A Page of Isolde's Logbook
relics.lore: Tin-box damp, a careful hand. 'The fen hears. Sat at the post till four. It is not the fish that listen, it is what the fish are for. I have stopped saying her name out loud here.'

hint.text: Dr. Calloway: 'There is a tin box at the Listening Post, by the stool. I have not opened it. You have the look of somebody it was left for.'

relics.name: The Stopped Watch
relics.lore: A keeper's watch on a tarred lanyard, stopped at ten to four. In a pocket it runs. Take it out and it is ten to four, and the second hand is just coming to rest.

hint.text: Cut into a pile of the Listening Post, low down: 'Lost my watch over the side here at ten to four. It will not be found by day. I. F.'

relics.name: The Return Half
relics.lore: The return half of a packet ticket, Sedge Landing to Hearthbay, never given up. Mister Hollis looked at it for some time and handed it back. 'I believe that is mine. Pray keep it. One of us should have somewhere to go back to.'

hint.text: Mister Hollis: 'I had the return half in my glove when I stepped down at the Landing. I have the glove still. I cannot answer for the ticket.'

relics.name: A Scrimshaw Tooth
relics.lore: A tooth as long as a forearm, cut fine with a sail needle: the lighthouse, lit, and two moons over it. On the root, B.O., and a year that has not come yet.

hint.text: Captain Oake: 'I'd a tooth I was cutting a picture on, forty years back. I let it fall in the Jaw's cove one night and never fished for it. I didn't care for what I'd drawn.'

relics.name: A Harpoon Head With a Ribbon
relics.lore: Never thrown: the edge is as the smith left it. A ribbon is tied through the eye in a bow, the way you would mark your place in a book.

hint.text: Captain Oake: 'The day I gave it up I let my best iron go over the side, under the Ribs. I tied a ribbon on it first. I couldn't tell you why. It seemed owed.'

relics.name: A Storm Glass
relics.lore: A sealed glass of cloudy spirit, meant to show tomorrow's weather. The crystals have set in the shape of a fork, and have not moved since it came up.

hint.text: Captain Oake: 'There was a storm glass on a post on the Anvil. Fenn's, I think. The Deacon had it off inside a week. It'll come up in weather or not at all.'

relics.name: A Boat's Nameboard
relics.lore: KEEPER'S FERRY, cut deep and gilded, off a boat nobody has built. Under it in pencil, in a careful hand: back by supper.

hint.text: Pell: 'There's a board adrift on the Long Swell at first light. Off my ferry. Not this one. The next. Don't ask me how. I only remember it.'

relics.name: A Third Page of Isolde's Logbook
relics.lore: Salt-stiff, written with a pencil kept on a string. 'The Reach breathes. In for nine, out for nine. I counted till dark and it never once hurried. Nothing that size is asleep by accident.'

hint.text: Captain Oake: 'There's a tin in the cairn at the Tally Stone. I've let it be forty years. It isn't for me.'
